subject: POC Observability Plan & Success Criteria — Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Johnson <alexa.johnson@fintechx.com>, Michael Perez <michael.perez@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC Observability Plan & Success Criteria — Recap from today's call

Hi Alexa / Michael,

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciated the thoughtful questions. Per our call, here's a concise recap and proposed next steps to get the POC moving: 

1) Success criteria (what FintechX will use to evaluate the POC):
   -  p99 request latency <= 120ms for 1-2k concurrent users (demo profile)
   -  Token-level cost within 20% of Redwood pre-run estimates for sample traffic
   -  No production data exfiltration; logs meet FintechX retention & redaction policy
   -  Ability to detect and alert on model regressions via quality test set (baseline BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity metrics)

2) Observability plan (what we'll surface during POC):
   - Dashboards: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec), error rates, token cost breakdown
   - Tracing: end-to-end distributed traces for sample request flows (client -> Redwood -> model), sampling at 100% for debug mode, 5% for baseline
   - Logs: structured request/response logs (redacted PII), KV cache hit rates, batching stats; export to FintechX's Cloud Logging (or S3)
   - Metrics to monitor: model output quality metrics (eval set scores), token consumption, batch sizes, queue times, GPU utilization, OOMs/restarts

3) Ownership & timeline
   - Redwood: provide observability dashboards + initial trace instrumentation + export connector (Marcus)

On Wed, Mar 4, 2026 at 09:12 AM Alexa Johnson <alexa.johnson@fintechx.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — that looks great.
>
> Two clarifications: 
> 1) For the POC evaluation, can we get a daily export of the structured logs (redacted) to our S3 bucket so our analytics team can run their own queries?
> 2) For model quality checks, we'd like automatic weekly snapshots of the eval-set outputs plus a small tool to re-run the eval locally. Is that possible during the 4-week POC?
>
> Proposed timeline: 4-week POC starting 2026-03-15, with a mid-point review week 2 and final review week 4.
>
> Happy to loop in Procurement this week to start SOW discussion.
>
> —Alexa
>
Alexa,

Quick replies inline below: 
- Daily export to S3: yes — we can configure structured log export to your S3-based ingestion with IAM role or presigned uploads. Marcus will send the connector details and permission requirements.
- Eval snapshots + local re-run tool: yes, we can schedule automated weekly eval exports and provide a small runner + instructions for your analytics team. We'll include the runner in the repo and provide a README for local evaluation.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus to share implementation details + required IAM/policy by EOD 3/5
- Redwood to share draft SOW for review (Marissa) by 3/6
- Align on final POC start date by 3/9

Regards,
Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan & Success Criteria — Implementation details

Thanks Marissa / Alexa — tagging on the technical bits: 

Implementation notes:
- Tracing: we'll instrument the request path with trace IDs propagated via X-Redwood-Trace header. For the POC, set sampling to 100% for the test cohort. We'll push traces to your Jaeger endpoint or to Redwood's tracing pipeline and forward exported traces to your collector.
- Logs: structured JSON entries with fields: request_id, user_id (hashed), route, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, error_code, model_version. PII fields will be redacted before export.
- Dashboards: Prebuilt Grafana dashboards (links below) for latency, throughput, token cost per route, and model quality trend. We'll provide dashboards as JSON for quick import.
- Metrics & alerts: set alerts for p99 latency > 150ms, error rate > 1%, GPU memory > 85% for sustained 5 mins, and model regression > 5% on eval metric.

Permissions: We'll need an IAM role with s3:PutObject for the designated bucket prefix. Alternatively, we can write to a presigned URL flow if that is preferable for security.

Deliverables & timeline (Marcus):
- 3/05 EOD: S3 export configuration + IAM policy (deliverable)
- 3/06: Grafana JSON dashboards + trace sampling config
- 3/10: Test harness to run evaluation locally + eval snapshots exporter

If you can confirm the S3 path and preferred auth method, I'll start the connector.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
